abstract: We introduce ceTDP, a two-stage framework for cluster-extent inference in neuroimaging that extends conventional random field theory-based and permutation-based methods. In contrast to standard cluster inference, which yields binary significance, ceTDP additionally quantifies the proportion of truly active voxels within clusters using the true discovery proportion (TDP). The method is built on closed testing and provides strong family-wise error rate control while remaining consistent with standard cluster inference. The framework operates in two stages: estimation of a cluster-extent threshold, followed by computation of the TDP lower bound. Two complementary procedures are provided: a conservative, statistically guaranteed TDP lower bound (ceTDP-cons) and a heuristic approach for obtaining a potentially tighter estimate of the TDP lower bound (ceTDP-heur). Together, they enable both rigorous inference and improved sensitivity in cluster-level analysis.
